answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pods in a four-player game. 2. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, next in B, and alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. 3. Put in the bag 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults at four players).
answers.evidence: [1] “2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players.” [2] “lowest-numbered pod in Section ‘A’, the next (in numerical order) in Section ‘B’, then alternate A/B”; “All pods start with their Locked side face up.” [3] “1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.”

answers.answer: 1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objectives marked for more players than the actual count; shuffle those decks separately and deal each player one of each face down. 2. Deal before Character draft. 3. At the First Encounter, when the first Intruder miniature appears, each player chooses one of the two and removes the other face down unseen. 4. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence: [1] “Remove from both Objective decks … all cards showing a player count higher than the actual number”; “Shuffle the two decks separately.” [2] “deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card … before the Character draft.” [3] “every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen).” [4] “Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.”

answers.answer: 1. Discard the used Action card and 2 additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. 2. With those cards, that is all four Action cards in hand; the two Contamination cards remain and cannot pay. 3. If the card has effects separated by OR, choose one effect.
answers.evidence: [1] “discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards.” [2] “Action Cost … discard exactly that many Action cards”; “Contamination cards … can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.” [3] “If a card has two sections separated by ‘OR,’ choose one.”

answers.answer: 1. A Character ending their own round in a burning Room takes 1 Light Wound then. 2. Passing bars further normal Actions this Player Phase. 3. When passing, they may discard any number of hand cards. 4. Fire wounds passing players only once at the end of their own round; later players' rounds do not cause further wounds to them that turn.
answers.evidence: [1] “ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound.” [2] “You cannot take further normal Actions.” [3] “At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.” [4] “Later players’ rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.”

answers.answer: 1. Flip the unexplored tile face up and set its Item count by rotating the tile so the Exploration token's number faces the board's Item Counter symbol (except Nest/Slime Room, which have no count). 2. Reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then remove it from play. 3. Unless its result replaces Noise, roll Noise only if the entered Room has no Character or Intruder; on 1–4 place a marker in the numbered connected Corridor, counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. 4. Silence cancels the roll; with Slime it becomes Danger. 5. Danger cancels the roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room; if none eligible, place Noise in every connected unmarked Corridor (including Technical when applicable). 6. If anyone is already in the destination Room, do not roll ordinary Movement Noise.
answers.evidence: [1] “rotate the Room tile until the token’s number faces the Item Counter symbol”; “Do not set an Item count for the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime.” [2] “flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token”; “remove it from the game.” [3] “Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered.” [4] “Silence — nothing happens; do NOT perform a Noise roll”; Slime makes it Danger. [5] “move ALL eligible Intruders”; if none “place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one.” [6] “If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.”

answers.answer: 1. It costs 2 Action cards. 2. On a move otherwise governed by normal movement rules, it replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing one Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination; the FAQ says this also overrides automatic Silence/Danger exploration results. 3. It cannot be used in Combat or if every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. 4. A Closed Door blocks passage. 5. A miniature can never stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: [1] “Careful Movement (cost 2).” [2] “instead of a Noise roll … place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor”; “replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results.” [3] “cannot … if all Corridors … already hold Noise”; “cannot use it while in Combat.” [4] “including Closed Doors blocking passage.” [5] “no one may ever stop in a Corridor.”

answers.answer: 1. Resolve an Encounter: discard all Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance); draw one token; place its matching miniature if not Blank; compare its number with the triggering player's hand. 2. Because the rolled Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead of adding a second marker. 3. The drawn non-Blank token is set aside outside the bag; it may return if that type later hides in Technical Corridors. 4. Fewer cards than the token number causes a Surprise Attack against the triggering Character; equal or more does not. 5. Both Action and Contamination cards in hand count for the comparison.
answers.evidence: [1] “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room”; then draw and place token; compare number. [2] “if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” [3] “Set the drawn token aside outside the bag.” [4] “Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack”; equal or more → nothing. [5] “Action AND Contamination cards both count.”

answers.answer: 1. Move all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room; eligibility excludes Intruders in Combat with any Character. 2. If there are none, put Noise in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including the Technical Corridors space if the Room has an Entrance. 3. An Intruder merely moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. 4. Slime makes Silence resolve as Danger.
answers.evidence: [1] “move ALL eligible Intruders.” [2] “If there are none … place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one.” [3] “An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter.” [4] “If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve ‘Danger’ instead.”

answers.answer: 1. In an Encounter, a Blank places Noise in each Corridor connected to that Room; no miniature appears and the Encounter ends. 2. Return the Blank to the bag. 3. If it was the last token in the bag, add one available Adult token (otherwise none). 4. By contrast, Blank drawn in bag development adds an Adult if available and returns to the bag; it does not itself state a Noise effect.
answers.evidence: [1] “place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room”; “Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” [2] “Return the Blank token to the bag.” [3] “If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token … (if any are available).” [4] Bag development: “Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag … Return the Blank token to the bag.”

answers.answer: 1. Both Intruders stay in their original Room when they attempt to move together through one Closed Door. 2. They destroy the Door; represent Destroyed by a lying token. 3. A Destroyed Door can never be Closed again by ordinary means. 4. An Intruder appearing because of a Noise roll comes through a Closed Door regardless; the Door does not block that appearance.
answers.evidence: [1] “several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put.” [2] “Destroyed = lying token.” [3] “can never be Closed again.” [4] “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”

answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed. 2. Discard all its Injury markers. 3. Return its token to the bag; a Noise marker on the shared Technical Corridors space remains. 4. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors, except Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item. 5. Doors can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: [1] “it disappears into the ducts.” [2] “discard all its Injury markers.” [3] “return its token to the Intruder bag”; “A Noise marker … is NOT removed.” [4] “Characters can never use them (the only exceptions …).” [5] “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

answers.answer: 1. Shoot costs 1 Action card and 1 Ammo, uses a Weapon in Hand, and targets one Intruder in your Room. 2. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, and targets one Intruder in your Room. 3. Shoot miss causes no Wound; Melee miss causes 1 Serious Wound. 4. Double-hit result deals 2 Injuries in Shoot, 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: [1] “Shoot (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo)”; “attack an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in your Hand.” [2] Melee: “draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile”; choose a target in your Room. [3] table: Blank Shoot “no Wound penalty”; Melee “suffer 1 Serious Wound.” [4] “Double-hit … 2 Injuries”; Melee “1 Injury.”

answers.answer: 1. A Larva dies at 1 Injury; remove it and place no Carcass. 2. An Adult's Injury Effect check draws one Intruder Attack card and compares its blood value with its current total Injuries; blood ≤ injuries kills it. 3. Queen draws two cards and sums blood; sum ≤ current injuries kills. 4. Dead Adult or Queen leaves a Carcass in the Room. 5. If either Queen check card shows a Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of numerical death/endurance; Queen retreats if either card has the symbol.
answers.evidence: [1] “Larva | 1 Injury kills”; “no Carcass.” [2] Adult: “Draw 1 Intruder Attack card”; “Blood ≤ Injuries kills.” [3] Queen: “Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values”; sum ≤ injuries kills. [4] Adult/Queen death: “place Carcass in Room.” [5] “Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol”; retreat instead of numerical result.

answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve the Escape attacks. 2. There is a separate attack per Intruder, starting with larger types: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; Escape attacks target the escaper. 3. If the Character dies, the Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. 4. If they survive, complete movement to the neighboring explored or unexplored Room; resolve exploration if needed and Noise normally if the destination is empty.
answers.evidence: [1] “BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack.” [2] “one separate Attack per Intruder … starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva)”; “Escape attack targets the escaper.” [3] “If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” [4] “If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored).”

answers.answer: 1. Among Characters in the Intruder's Room, target the player with the fewest Action cards; on a tie choose First Player or next in turn order. Surprise Attack instead targets the Encounter-triggering Character. 2. A non-Larva draws one Intruder Attack card; matching Intruder symbol means resolve its effect, otherwise miss; ignore blood. 3. Larva draws no Attack card. 4. Remove Larva miniature and place it on target's Character board; target gains a Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile. If target already has Larva, attacking Larva disappears, existing Larva stays, and target only gains the card.
answers.evidence: [1] “FEWEST Action cards in hand”; tie “First Player token (or the next player in turn order)”; Surprise Attack targets triggerer. [2] “if it shows a symbol matching … resolve”; otherwise misses; “Ignore the blood icon.” [3] “Larva exception: draw no Attack card.” [4] “place it on the target’s Character board”; “target gains 1 Contamination card”; already-Larva exception states existing one stays and only card gained.

requested_parts: dressed Serious Wound and death threshold
Corpse and Heavy Objects on death
answers.answer: 1. Dressing a Serious Wound only ignores its effect; it still counts toward the three-wound limit. At 3 Serious Wounds, any additional Wound kills, even if one is dressed. 2. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and becomes a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as specified by the healing effect. 4. On death, place Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there; Item cards disappear from the game.
answers.evidence: [1] “Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds.” [2] “on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” [3] “Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card.” [4] Corpse token is placed in Room and “drop all their Heavy Objects there”; FAQ says Item cards “disappear from the game.”

answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower optionally scan all Contamination cards in your HAND; remove non-Infected scanned cards from game. 2. Infected cards are kept; with no Larva place a Larva, and with one already present the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. 3. Surgery scans all Contamination in deck, hand and discard, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva if present. 4. Then suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, shuffle all cards including hand into Action deck; hand remains empty until next turn. No new Contamination card is given.
answers.evidence: [1] Canteen/Shower: “Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones.” [2] scan table: Infected retained; place Larva or death/Creeper if Larva already there. [3] Surgery: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva.” [4] “suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass”; shuffle all cards “including the entire hand”; “hand stays empty until the next turn.”

answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys one uncarried Egg; a successful Egg Melee still draws Contamination, but a missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound (timing reconciliation is unresolved). 2. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov destroys 1 immediately and its Fire can destroy later; a Fire marker destroys 1 each Event Phase, or 2 Nest Eggs per step with Vulnerability to Fire. 3. Egg Melee retains the ordinary Contamination draw on success; miss waives it and Wound. 4. Roll Noise after every Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt, including a miss; remote grenade/molotov rolls Noise in your own Room. 5. When no Eggs remain on the Intruder board, Nest is destroyed; mark with 1 Injury.
answers.evidence: [1] “Each Injury destroys 1 Egg”; “Successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw”; “missed … neither Contamination nor a Wound”; timing “unresolved.” [2] Grenade “Destroys 2 Eggs”; Molotov “Destroys 1 Egg”; Fire destroys “1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase”; Vulnerability = 2 Nest Eggs. [3] Same Egg Melee statements. [4] “after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt … including a miss”; remote roll “in your own Room.” [5] “When no Eggs remain … Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.”

answers.answer: 1. Pay 2 cards for the matching Evacuation Section Room Action. Pod must be Unlocked with space; no entry if Section has an Intruder or Malfunction. 2. Roll Noise first; if an Intruder is present or appears, attempt fails; otherwise board. 3. Each Pod fits 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 4. After boarding you may launch immediately, or wait and pass the current turn. At the start of your first round each later Player Phase choose one: continue waiting and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and take a full 2-Action round. Waiting Characters count as present in Section for bag-development Noise; Intruder appearing there returns Pod occupants to Section Room; Malfunction arising while waiting still allows wait/launch/exit but blocks new entry.
answers.evidence: [1] “pay 2 Action cards”; “No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction.” [2] “First roll Noise”; appearance/reach “makes entry fail.” [3] “2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space.” [4] “Launch immediately”; otherwise “pass the current turn”; later round choices exactly listed. Waiting occupants “treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls”; Intruder returns them; Malfunction permits wait, launch or exit.

answers.answer: 1. Victory checks run Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives. 2. Two Damaged Engines make ship explode; everything aboard dies, but launched Pod passengers are away. 3. Non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters, except a sleeper with Quarantine Objective survives at Mars; ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. 4. For every surviving Character: without an existing Larva, scan all Contamination in Action deck, hand, discard. If any scan is Infected, or Larva already exists, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards across deck/hand/discard and draw top 4; any Contamination among four kills regardless of infection status. 5. Launched Pod passengers undergo the same final Contamination and Objective checks.
answers.evidence: [1] “Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives.” [2] “2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies”; “Launched Pod passengers are already away.” [3] “Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters”; Quarantine sleeper survives “if the destination is Mars.” [4] Full endgame rule gives scan zones and trigger; “Any Contamination card in those four, whether Infected or not, kills.” [5] “every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers.”

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle all Room 2 tiles unseen, put one face down in each marked 2 slot and return extras; do the same with all Room 1 tiles. Put one shuffled face-down Exploration token on each tile; return extras. 2. Place one random face-down Coordinates card by Cockpit; Destination marker starts on B; Time marker starts on green space. 3. For each Engine, shuffle one Working and one Damaged token face down and stack them on its slot; top token is true status. 4. Put 5 Egg tokens and 3 random face-down Weakness cards in Intruder board slots.
answers.evidence: [1] “Shuffle all Room tiles ‘2’ … one face down on each … slot marked ‘2’”; likewise Room 1; “one [Exploration token] face down on each Room tile.” [2] “1 random Coordinates card”; Destination marker on “B”; Time marker on green. [3] “1 Damaged, 1 Working,” shuffle and stack; top indicates true status. [4] “5 Egg tokens and 3 random Weakness cards face down.”

answers.answer: 1. Randomly deal Help cards numbered 1 through player count; number on Help/Inventory is Player Number and controls draft order. 2. Shuffle Character draft cards; Player 1 draws 2 publicly, keeps 1 and shuffles other back; repeat in player-number order. 3. Each gets Character board/miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10-card Action deck, Starting Weapon in a Hand slot loaded to capacity, and two Quest Items horizontal/inactive beside board. 4. Blue Character Corpse token begins in Hibernatorium as dead crew Object. 5. Quest Items are not active at start; unlock through mini-quests.
answers.evidence: [1] “number on Help card and Inventory is the Player Number”; sets character-choice order. [2] Player 1 draws 2, “reveals both choices publicly,” keeps 1, shuffles other back; then Player 2 etc. [3] setup lists components and placement; Weapon “loaded with Ammo markers equal to … capacity”; Quest Items horizontal. [4] “Place the blue Character Corpse token in the Hibernatorium.” [5] “NOT active at the start — they unlock via mini-quests.”

answers.answer: 1. At Player Phase start every player draws to hand of 5. 2. After drawing, pass First Player token left except first game turn. 3. If Action deck is empty when required to draw, shuffle discard into a new deck then draw. 4. Card discards are face up: used Action cards to own Action discard; Contamination atop it; Items to matching discard; Event, Attack and Serious Wound cards to respective discards. Normal card discards are face up. Gained Contamination cannot be paid as Action cost. Special Search/Storage rejected Item goes face down to bottom of chosen deck.
answers.evidence: [1] “draw … up to a hand of 5 cards.” [2] “after drawing, pass the token … (do NOT pass it on the first turn).” [3] “Whenever you must draw and your Action deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck.” [4] “Normal card discards are face up”; discard table names destinations; Search/Storage return other card “face down to the bottom” of chosen deck.

answers.answer: 1. Advance Time (and active Self-Destruct), Intruder Attacks, Fire Damage and Injury Effect checks, then resolve Event card. 2. Move all Intruders with the card's symbol that are not in a Room with any Character. 3. Movement uses neighboring Corridor matching the card's number; Technical number returns token to bag/removes miniature. Then resolve event effect and discard card unless specified otherwise. 4. If Event deck empties, shuffle its discards into new deck. 5. If Intruder Attack deck empties, reshuffle its discard into new deck.
answers.evidence: [1] Turn structure numbered steps 4–7 in this order. [2] “all Intruders showing the card’s Intruder symbol that are NOT in a Room with any Characters move.” [3] “through the Corridor matching the number”; Technical Corridors return token; “after the movement step, resolve the effect.” [4] Event deck “shuffle the Event discards into a new deck.” [5] Attack deck: “if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck.”

answers.answer: 1. Larva: remove from bag and add an Adult. 2. Creeper: remove and add a Breeder. 3. Adult: return it immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Combat; Encounters may draw same Adult. 4. Breeder: all players roll Noise in order, skipping Combat; then return Breeder. 5. Queen: if Character(s) in Nest place Queen and resolve Encounter; otherwise, or Nest undiscovered, add Egg to Intruder board; return Queen. 6. Only Adult/Breeder branches call for Noise rolls, by all players in order except Combat. 7. A new turn begins only after all bag development and resulting Encounters/Surprise Attacks resolve.
answers.evidence: [1] “Larva — remove this token from the bag; add 1 Adult token.” [2] “Creeper — remove … add 1 Breeder.” [3] Adult “return the token … immediately before all players roll for Noise”; skip Combat; Encounter may draw same Adult. [4] Breeder rolls then return. [5] Queen branch exactly stated; return token. [6] Adult and Breeder directions. [7] “turn only ends once the bag development step is fully resolved (all Encounters, Surprise Attacks, etc.).”

answers.answer: 1. Attempting to place a ninth Fire marker ends game by ship explosion. 2. Attempting ninth Malfunction marker ends game by hull integrity loss/explosion. 3. Max one of each marker per Room; extra placement does nothing. Discarded markers return to appropriate pool. 4. On hull loss all Characters aboard, awake or hibernated, die. 5. Everything else aboard, including Intruders, dies too.
answers.evidence: [1] “if instructed to place a 9th Fire marker … ship explodes.” [2] “9th Malfunction marker … ship loses hull integrity and the game ends.” [3] “Max 1 per Room”; “discarded markers return to the pool.” [4] “ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die.” [5] “everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders.”

answers.answer: 1. A Malfunction disables that Room's Action and Computer; Special Rooms are affected too. 2. Searching still works in a Malfunctioning Room. 3. Malfunctions cannot be placed in Nest, Room Covered With Slime, or unexplored Rooms. 4. It never changes an Engine token/status. 5. A Hibernatorium Malfunction does not affect already-hibernating Characters.
answers.evidence: [1] “Room’s Action is unavailable”; “A Malfunction makes a Room’s Computer unavailable.” [2] “Searching still works.” [3] “Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime”; “cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms.” [4] “Engine status is never affected.” [5] “doesn’t affect already-hibernated Characters.”

answers.answer: 1. Normal Item cards in Inventory are hidden; others see only backs/colors. 2. No Inventory size limit; show any Item when used. 3. Heavy Items and Objects are visible and occupy one of two Hand slots, maximum two; Heavy Objects include Eggs, Character Corpses and Intruder Carcasses. Heavy Items found by Search need no separate Pick Up Action; searched Weapons start with 1 Ammo, capped at capacity. 4. Add-type Items attach and act as one; Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items into one slot, never Objects.
answers.evidence: [1] “keeps non-Heavy Item cards hidden”; “others see only card backs/colors.” [2] “No Inventory size limit”; “Any Item used must be shown.” [3] Heavy Items/Objects “must occupy one of your 2 Hand slots”; searched Weapons “loaded with 1 Ammo.” [4] “Add-type Items … attach”; “Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy ITEMS into 1 Hand slot (never Objects).”

requested_parts: searched Weapon Ammo vs starting Weapon
answers.answer: 1. Dropped Objects remain in the Room; dropped Item cards are lost/discarded. 2. Drop freely at any time during your turn without spending an Action. 3. A Weapon found by Search comes with 1 Ammo; Starting Weapon comes loaded to its printed Ammo capacity.
answers.evidence: [1] “Dropped Objects stay in the Room; dropped Items are lost (discarded).” [2] “free, any time during your turn, no Action.” [3] Found Weapons “loaded with 1 Ammo”; starting Weapon “loaded with Ammo markers equal to … capacity.”

answers.answer: 1. Search the deck matching Room color: Red, Yellow or Green; white Room allows choice of any three. Blue Crafted Items are never found by Search. 2. Draw 2 from one deck, keep 1, put other face down at bottom of that deck. 3. Each Search reduces Room Item Counter by 1. 4. At zero ordinary Search is unavailable (Scout Scavenging exception). 5. Nest and Room Covered With Slime prohibit any Search; Storage Room Action is a separate draw-two search-like effect, and Blue Items only via Crafting.
answers.evidence: [1] “drawn must match the searched Room’s color”; white choose any 3; Blue “never found by searching.” [2] “draws 2 cards … keeps 1 … bottom of that deck.” [3] “Each Search lowers … Item Counter by 1.” [4] “at 0 … cannot be searched (exception: Scout’s Scavenging).” [5] Nest/Slime “explicitly prohibit any Search Action”; Crafted deck items taken only through Craft Item Action.

answers.answer: 1. Craft Item Basic Action discards 2 Item cards whose blue Component icons match the Crafted card's two gray icons. 2. The crafted card must be available; matching components do not suffice if none is available. 3. You may inspect the Craft deck at any time. 4. Four items/components: Antidote flame + medical cross; Taser battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: [1] “discard 2 Item cards showing the appropriate blue Craft (Component) icons.” [2] “cannot be built if its card is not available.” [3] “may look through the Craft deck at any time.” [4] listed crafted item symbol pairs as quoted.

answers.answer: 1. Only Trade initiator pays the Action cost. 2. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including non-initiators; exchange only if both parties agree. 3. You may give an Item/Object for nothing; do not spend an empty Action without intention to trade, though honest negotiation may end without exchange. 4. Characters cannot exchange Ammo. 5. Heavy Items found by Searching do not need a separate Pick Up Action; that Action is for Objects only.
answers.evidence: [1] “Only the initiator spends the Action.” [2] “trade with all Characters in your Room”; FAQ any Characters “including pairs who did not initiate/pay.” [3] “You may give … for nothing”; empty Actions “with no intention” disallowed; honest negotiations may end without trade. [4] “Characters cannot exchange Ammo.” [5] “Heavy Items found by Searching do not require this Action — it applies to Objects only.”

answers.answer: 1. Weaknesses correspond to Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass or Egg Objects present for Analyse; the specific matching Object/card pairing is implied by the corresponding Weakness. 2. Object must be in Laboratory Room. 3. It is not consumed. 4. Reveal matching Weakness face up on Intruder board; its rule benefits all players. 5. Anyone may research; Discover Weakness Objective does not require you personally to do so.
answers.evidence: [1] “Analyse 1 Object (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg …): reveal the corresponding Weakness card.” [2] “present in the Room” (Laboratory); Intranet still requires “Object itself in the Laboratory.” [3] “Object is not consumed.” [4] “leave it on the Intruder board. Its rule benefits all players.” [5] Objective guidance: “corresponding Object must be researched in the Laboratory by anyone.” Exact per-card mapping is not specified in this summary.

answers.answer: 1. Room Action costs 2 Action cards; must be in the Room, out of Combat and without a Malfunction there unless an explicit ability overrides location. 2. A Computer icon alone has no stated effect; Computers are usable as a condition for specific actions, but a Malfunction disables the Computer. 3. Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching; a Room's Fire marker remains unless an effect removes it.
answers.evidence: [1] “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use”; cost 2; cannot use in Combat or Malfunction. [2] Malfunction “makes a Room’s Computer unavailable”; no independent Computer-icon effect is described in summary. [3] “Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms.”

answers.answer: 1. Armory adds Ammo only to Energy Weapons, not Classic Weapons. 2. It adds 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons. 3. Cannot exceed weapon capacity; common Room Action requirements apply (present, out of Combat, no Malfunction, cost 2 cards).
answers.evidence: [1] “add 2 Ammo to 1 of your Energy Weapons (never Classic Weapons).” [2] “add 2 Ammo.” [3] “never above capacity”; Room Actions common requirements state cost and restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. Choose one of: Dress all Serious Wounds; Heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound; or Heal all Light Wounds. 2. Dressing flips a Serious Wound card face down and ignores its effect; it remains a wound and is not removed. 3. Duplicate Serious Wound cards are not cumulative, though they are harder to remove.
answers.evidence: [1] Emergency Room: “Dress ALL your Serious Wounds OR Heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound OR Heal all your Light Wounds.” [2] “Dressing does not prevent death”; “it still counts toward the 3-wound limit.” [3] “Duplicate Serious Wound cards are NOT cumulative.”

answers.answer: 1. Sending a Signal places a Status marker on your board's Signal space. 2. It is used only for Objectives. 3. Comms Room is always aboard, so it cannot be absent from a normal game.
answers.evidence: [1] “Send a Signal: place a Status marker on your board’s Signal space.” [2] “only used for Objectives.” [3] Objective guidance: “a Comms Room is always aboard.”

answers.answer: 1. Fire Control chooses any one Room and discards its Fire marker if present. 2. All Intruders there run away in random directions, drawing one Event card per Intruder. 3. It works even if the chosen Room has no Fire, still scattering its Intruders.
answers.evidence: [1] “choose any 1 Room: discard its Fire marker (if any).” [2] “ALL Intruders there run away in random directions (draw 1 Event card per Intruder).” [3] “Works even with no Fire, to scatter Intruders.”

answers.answer: 1. Generator starts sequence by placing marker on first green space; stopping removes it, and restarting begins again at green. Characters cannot initiate while anyone is hibernating; Coolant Leak Event can. 2. Advance Self-Destruct one space whenever Time advances. 3. At first yellow it cannot be stopped and all Pods unlock; later yellow spaces do not unlock again even if relocked. 4. Final skull space explodes ship. 5. If hyperspace jump occurs while active, ship is still considered destroyed. 6. Characters cannot start sequence while a Character already hibernates; Event exception applies.
answers.evidence: [1] “Starting … first (green) space”; “stop … removes marker (a new sequence restarts from green)”; hibernation restriction and Coolant Leak exception. [2] marker advances “every time the Time marker advances.” [3] “first yellow”; cannot abort; Pods unlock; later spaces do not unlock. [4] final skull: “ship explodes.” [5] “If a hyperspace jump happens while Self-Destruct is active, the ship is still considered destroyed.” [6] Characters “cannot start … while any Character is hibernating.”

answers.answer: 1. Airlock Control targets any one OTHER Yellow Room (not the Airlock Control Room itself). 2. Its connected Corridors must contain no Destroyed Doors. 3. Close every Door around it and place Airlock Procedure token there. 4. If all those Doors remain Closed until current Player Phase ends (all players passed), everything in Room dies and any Fire is removed. Opening any Door first cancels procedure.
answers.evidence: [1] “pick any 1 OTHER Yellow Room.” [2] “whose connected Corridors contain no Destroyed Doors.” [3] “automatically Close every Door around it and place the Airlock Procedure token.” [4] “If all … still Closed when current Player Phase ends … everything … dies”; “if any … opened first, … cancelled.”

answers.answer: 1. At start of a new turn, a Character in Cabins with no Intruder present draws one extra Action card, for hand of 6 instead of 5. 2. Malfunction disables this passive. 3. It is not a paid Room Action; it is passive.
answers.evidence: [1] “at the start of a new turn … draws 1 extra Action card (hand of 6 instead of 5).” [2] “Disabled by a Malfunction token.” [3] “passive.”

answers.answer: 1. Command Center may choose any one Room, including a distant one. 2. You choose which Doors in that Room's connected Corridors to open or close. 3. Destroyed Doors cannot normally be closed again, so Command Center cannot close them.
answers.evidence: [1] “choose any 1 Room.” [2] “Open/Close any of the Doors … (your choice which).” [3] Destroyed Door “can never be Closed again (only exception: Plasma Torch Item).”

answers.answer: 1. Engine Control Room checks status of all three Engines but cannot change status. 2. A Malfunction in an Engine Room does not prevent this check. It disables that Room's action and does not change Engine token/status.
answers.evidence: [1] “check the status of all 3 Engines”; “cannot CHANGE Engine status here.” [2] “works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker”; Room Malfunction affects only Room Action, not Engine status.

answers.answer: 1. Hatch Control flips one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. 2. Monitoring inspects one unexplored Room tile. 3. It secretly looks at tile and its Exploration token together. 4. Replace them face down; you may lie about what you saw. It does not inspect an explored tile per the summary.
answers.evidence: [1] “flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked.” [2] Monitoring: “any 1 unexplored Room tile.” [3] “and its Exploration token.” [4] “secretly”; “then replace them (you may lie about what you saw).”

answers.answer: 1. Entering Room Covered With Slime automatically gives Slime; no separate Action is needed. 2. It has no Item count and cannot receive Malfunction. 3. Slime max 1; further Slime has no additional effect. 4. Shower removes Slime, not Fire; Fire may exist there normally and is not extinguished by showering.
answers.evidence: [1] “entering automatically gives you a Slime marker.” [2] “no Item count is set here”; Malfunction “can never be placed here.” [3] “Max 1 (further Slime does nothing).” [4] Shower: “discard your Slime marker”; “Fire … is NOT removed by showering.”

answers.answer: 1. Cockpit lets you secretly check Coordinates and replace/remember them, or set Destination by moving marker. 2. You may lie about Coordinates information. 3. Destination marker selects one of four entries on Coordinates card, indicating jump destination. 4. You cannot change Destination once anyone hibernates. 5. You cannot set Destination with an Intruder in Cockpit.
answers.evidence: [1] “Check Coordinates (secretly look …) … OR Set Destination.” [2] “you may lie; replace it and remember it.” [3] “marker selects one of the four destination entries.” [4] “change Destination once anyone is hibernating.” [5] “never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit.”

answers.answer: 1. Checking an Engine secretly views its top token; repair/break secretly examines both tokens and restacks them in chosen order. 2. You may lie about check; you need not say whether repair occurred. 3. You must announce if you changed token order. 4. No prior check or functioning Engine Room is required; Repair/Break works despite Malfunction and may be done with appropriate Repairs Action or Tools Item.
answers.evidence: [1] Check “secretly look at the TOP token”; Repair/Break “secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order.” [2] “you may lie”; “needn’t say whether you repaired it.” [3] “MUST say if you changed the order.” [4] “Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first.”

requested_parts: hibernation legal timing and room conditions
answers.answer: 1. Hibernation requires Time on a blue space, be in Hibernatorium, no Intruder and no Malfunction there; pay 2 cards. 2. Roll Noise; an Intruder appearing/reaching Room makes attempt fail. 3. Otherwise remove miniature and stop participating until end checks. 4. Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains exception. 5. Later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake or harm sleeper.
answers.evidence: [1] “pay 2 Action cards”; “Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction.” [2] “Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing … makes the attempt fail.” [3] “remove your miniature and stop participating.” [4] “Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character.” [5] “later … Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers.”

answers.answer: 1. When Time marker reaches final red space, ship jumps immediately; awake Characters aboard die from g-force. 2. Game also ends when last alive non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates or launches; then force Self-Destruct marker to final red if active, otherwise Time to final red, and resolve effects. 3. Active Self-Destruct is therefore resolved by ship destruction. 4. Intruders are unharmed by normal hyperspace jump.
answers.evidence: [1] “Time marker reaches the final red space … ship jumps … every Character … not hibernating dies.” [2] last active Character condition and forced-track rule. [3] “move [Self-Destruct] marker to its final red space; … resolve those effects.” [4] “Intruders are unharmed by the hyperjump.”

answers.answer: 1. Characters cannot directly attack another Character. 2. They can indirectly harm others, including locking them in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct with people aboard, or throwing a Grenade into a Room with crew.
answers.evidence: [1] “Characters can never directly attack other Characters.” [2] “harm them indirectly: locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct with people aboard, throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew.”

requested_parts: Intruder entering unexplored Room by movement
answers.answer: 1. If all eight Adult models are on board, remove all Adult models not in Combat and return their tokens to bag if possible, then place Adult in Encounter Room. If all eight are in Combat, summary explicitly says procedure unresolved; authoritative clarification needed. 2. Intruder movement into unexplored Room does not remove it and does not reveal Room tile or Exploration token.
answers.evidence: [1] “if all 8 models are on the board, the Adults retreat — remove all Adult models NOT in Combat and return their tokens to the bag (if possible)”; if all eight in Combat, “source does not explain how to supply the required model.” [2] “do not remove it and do not reveal the Room or its Exploration token.”

requested_parts: same symbols in Melee for ineligible target
answers.answer: 1. Small curled symbol inflicts 1 Injury only on Larva/Creeper; against Adult, Breeder or Queen it misses. 2. Larger curved symbol hits Larva/Creeper/Adult for 1 Injury; misses Breeder/Queen. 3. Melee uses same restrictions; an ineligible target is a miss and causes attacker 1 Serious Wound.
answers.evidence: [1] table: “Small curled … 1 Injury to Larva/Creeper; miss against other types.” [2] “Larger curved … Larva/Creeper/Adult; miss against Breeder/Queen.” [3] Melee: “ineligible target means miss and 1 Serious Wound.”

requested_parts: final check no Larva/all scans negative
earlier launched Pod and Objective check
answers.answer: 1. With no Larva, scan every Contamination card in Action deck, hand and discard. 2. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw; non-Infected cards are not removed by this endgame procedure. 3. Pod passengers still face final Contamination and Objective checks, even if launched earlier.
answers.evidence: [1] “No Larva already on board: Scan every Contamination card from Action deck, hand and discard pile.” [2] “If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw”; “does not remove cards merely because they scanned non-Infected.” [3] “including launched Pod passengers”; they “still face the final Contamination and Objective checks.”

answers.answer: 1. Antidote: flame + medical cross. 2. Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3. Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool. 4. Molotov Cocktail: flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: [1] “Antidote = flame + medical cross.” [2] “Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool.” [3] “Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool.” [4] “Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric.”

requested_parts: In Combat Only/Out of Combat Only
answers.answer: 1. In Combat whenever an Intruder is in your Room; Eggs do not count. 2. In Combat Only can be used only with Intruder in Room; Out of Combat Only only when none. 3. Unmarked Action or Item Action may be used in either situation if other requirements met; Basic and Room Actions have separate limitations. 4. Eggs do not cause Combat.
answers.evidence: [1] “in Combat whenever an Intruder is in your Room”; “Eggs do not count as Intruders.” [2] table defines markings. [3] “No Combat marking … either situation”; Basic and Room Actions retain separate limits. [4] same Eggs-do-not-count quotation.

answers.answer: 1. For 'Player X cannot survive,' that Character must be dead at game end; you need not kill them personally. 2. Hibernating or escaping means they survived, so neither counts as death. 3. 'Only survivor' means no other Character may survive. 4. Regardless of Objective, your own Character must survive by Pod or hibernation.
answers.evidence: [1] “that Character must simply be dead … you don’t have to kill them with your own Actions.” [2] “not hibernated, not escaped.” [3] “no other Character may survive.” [4] “Regardless of Objective, your Character must survive.”

answers.answer: 1. If Door pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board. 2. Open is no token; Closed is standing token; Destroyed is lying token. 3. Maximum one Door per Corridor. 4. No Door tokens in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: [1] “If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board.” [2] “Open = no token”; “Closed = standing”; “Destroyed = lying.” [3] “max 1 per Corridor.” [4] “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: first death effect on all Pods
answers.answer: 1. On first Character death, all Escape Pods automatically unlock immediately. 2. They may subsequently be Locked or Unlocked normally, such as via Hatch Control; the summary says later deaths re-unlocking after relocking is unresolved due conflicting wording, but no need for first death rule itself.
answers.evidence: [1] “all Escape Pods are automatically Unlocked (flip tokens).” [2] “For the rest of the game they may be Locked/Unlocked normally”; source limitations note whether later deaths re-unlock Pods after first unlock was reversed is unresolved.

answers.answer: 1. Storage Room Action draws two cards from a chosen Red/Yellow/Green Item deck and keeps one. 2. Return rejected card face down to bottom of that chosen deck. 3. Room Action costs 2 Action cards; must be in that Room, out of Combat and without Malfunction there, unless explicit ability exception.
answers.evidence: [1] Storage: “draw 2 cards from a chosen Item deck (Red/Yellow/Green), keep 1.” [2] “other to the bottom of that deck.” [3] common Room Action requirements: “in the Room … outside Combat … no Malfunction”; “Pay 2 Action cards.”

answers.answer: 1. In Nest, use Nest Room Action to take 1 Egg token from Intruder board. 2. Pay 2 Action cards. 3. Then make a Noise roll. 4. A previously taken/dropped Egg in your Room is a normal Heavy Object and uses Basic Pick Up Heavy Object for 1 card; the basic pickup does not call for Noise. A dropped Egg does not restore Nest Egg total.
answers.evidence: [1] Nest: “take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board.” [2] Room Actions cost 2. [3] Nest action says “then make a Noise roll.” [4] “Pick Up Heavy Object … (cost 1 Action card)”; “no Noise-roll instruction”; dropped Egg is “normal Heavy Object” and doesn't restore Nest total.

requested_parts: One Use Only disposition after action
answers.answer: 1. Discard the One Use Only Item card after use, in addition to paying its Action-card cost.
answers.evidence: “One Use Only Items are discarded after use.” Table: “One Use Only — discard after use.”

requested_parts: Pod passenger arrival location for Character rule
answers.answer: 1. Character in a launched Escape Pod counts as arriving on Earth. 2. This does not establish the ship reached Earth; it establishes the passenger's arrival treatment only.

requested_parts: Noise roll while waiting during Adult development
answers.answer: 1. Yes. A waiting Pod occupant is treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development, so they roll when Adult development calls for all players to roll (unless in Combat; a waiting passenger is not described as in Combat).
answers.evidence: “You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development.” Adult branch says “all players roll for Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat).”

answers.answer: 1. You may launch. 2. You may keep waiting. 3. You may exit to the Section Room. 4. Section Malfunction blocks only new Pod entry; it does not bar these options for a passenger already waiting.
answers.evidence: “A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait: you may still wait, launch or exit”; “marker blocks only new entry to Pods.”

answers.answer: 1. One separate Intruder Attack for every Intruder in the Room. 2. Resolve largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.
answers.evidence: “one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva).”

requested_parts: remove-self Event with unresolvable other effect
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Remove an Event that instructs removal from game even if its other effect cannot be resolved.
answers.evidence: “Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve.”

answers.answer: 1. Return drawn Adult token to bag immediately before all players roll Noise. 2. Yes, a Noise-triggered Encounter can draw that same Adult token.
answers.evidence: Adult is “return[ed] … immediately before all players roll for Noise”; “An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token.”

answers.answer: 1. Normally the retreating Intruder destroys Closed Door and stays in place. 2. With The Way of Moving Weakness, affected Intruder other than Breeder/Queen does nothing at that Door (it neither moves nor destroys it).
answers.evidence: “A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays.” Under Weakness affected “other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door.”

requested_parts: Hand Serious Wound effect on Basic Shoot
answers.answer: 1. No. Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost. 2. Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action, which is the category Hand modifies.
answers.evidence: “Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.”

answers.answer: 1. Vulnerability to Fire adds 1 Injury per damage instance (x+1), not one per each Injury in a multi-Injury hit. 2. Flamethrower two-crosshair hit deals 3 Injuries total.

answers.answer: 1. Remove attacking Larva from board and place it on target Character board if target has none. 2. If target already has Larva, attacking one disappears and existing Larva stays. 3. Target gains 1 Contamination card but is not automatically killed by this attack.
answers.evidence: Infest: “remove the Larva miniature … place it on the target’s Character board”; with existing Larva “attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays”; “only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them.”

answers.answer: 1. Sleeper in Hibernatorium does not take later Fire wounds there. 2. Ship destruction still kills hibernating Characters; endgame survival checks, including Coordinates and Contamination, also still apply and may eliminate them.
answers.evidence: “A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium.” “ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter.” Endgame Coordinates: non-Earth kills hibernators; Contamination check kills on stated conditions.

requested_parts: Coolant Leak can start with sleeper
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates. 2. A Character may not start it once anyone is hibernating; the Event is an explicit exception.
answers.evidence: “Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers.” “Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating.”

answers.answer: 1. Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to unused token pool beside board. 2. They remain reusable; they are not removed permanently.
answers.evidence: “Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently.”

answers.answer: 1. Fire markers may be placed in unexplored Rooms. 2. Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms.
answers.evidence: “Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can.”

requested_parts: remaining Wounds after two more Lights at two Lights
answers.answer: 1. First Light wound converts existing two Light Wounds into one Serious Wound and clears Light track; second new Light wound remains. Final: one Serious Wound and one Light Wound.
answers.evidence: “Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound.”

answers.answer: 1. Heavy Objects drop in the Room where Character dies. 2. Item cards disappear from game; they do not drop as Objects.
answers.evidence: “Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game.”

requested_parts: second yellow space after Pods relocked
answers.answer: 1. No. Pods unlock automatically only when Self-Destruct first reaches a yellow space; after relocking, reaching later yellow spaces does not unlock them again.
answers.evidence: “first yellow space … Pods unlock”; “later yellow spaces do not unlock them again.”

requested_parts: ship destruction and kill Queen/destroy Nest Objectives
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Ship destruction fulfills requirements to kill Queen or destroy Nest because all Intruders die. 2. It does not alone make your Character a winner: Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective.

answers.answer: 1. No, an empty Trade Action with no intention of exchange should be disallowed. 2. If players genuinely negotiate, they may end without completing a trade.

answers.answer: 1. Activate Quest Item using the Basic Action printed on its card (illustrated activations cost 1). 2. It is forbidden in Combat. 3. A Room Malfunction does not prevent activation.
answers.evidence: “Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room.”

answers.answer: 1. Basic Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape are allowed in Combat. 2. Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object and Quest Item activation are not allowed. 3. Action-card or Item Actions may be used in either Combat state if unmarked, or if their marking and own requirements permit; Room Actions are forbidden in Combat.
answers.evidence: “Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape”; list excludes Trade, Craft, Pick Up, Quest activation. Unmarked Action/Item may be used either situation; Room Actions forbidden.

requested_parts: Noise and Surprise target with two Characters
answers.answer: 1. Soldier may use Covering Fire to move themselves alone. 2. When moving two Characters, each chooses their direction. 3. Perform one Noise roll; if an Encounter results, compare Surprise against Soldier (not the other Character).
answers.evidence: “Soldier may use it for themselves alone.” “Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier.”

answers.answer: 1. Full Auto damage is Shoot result plus half the Ammo discarded rounded down, plus Assault Rifle's +1 bonus. 2. Discard all Ammo from Assault Rifle before performing one Shoot Action.
answers.evidence: “remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action”; damage adds Shoot result, “half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle’s +1 bonus.”

answers.answer: 1. You may see Intruder Attack card before choosing Nerves of Steel. 2. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still suffer applicable effects such as Frenzy.
answers.evidence: “you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it.” “It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits.”

answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement overrides automatic Danger/Silence Exploration results and places its chosen Noise instead. 2. Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.
answers.evidence: “Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.”

answers.answer: 1. Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. 2. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat. 3. That movement uses normal Escape rules, including Intruder attacks before moving, one per Intruder.
answers.evidence: “Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat.” “Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape.” Escape rule states attack per Intruder before moving.

answers.answer: 1. Motivation with active Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room.
answers.evidence: “Motivation with Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room.”

requested_parts: Door exploration through Technical Corridor entry
answers.answer: 1. Ignore a Door Exploration token when entering via Technical Corridors Action card or Technical Corridor Plans Item, because the entry Corridor cannot be determined; no Door is placed.

answers.answer: 1. No. You must be in the same Room as the Character performing interrupted Action; cannot Interrupt remote Order via Intercom from elsewhere. 2. Passing does not bar Interruption; it remains permitted after passing subject to requirements.
answers.evidence: “remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere”; “Interruption may still be played after passing,” but requires same Room.

requested_parts: empty hand after two Actions and passing
answers.answer: 1. No. Empty hand after completing two Actions does not automatically make you pass; wait for your next round. 2. That extra round may incur another Fire or Bleeding effect before you pass.
answers.evidence: “An empty hand does not automatically make you pass after completing 2 Actions. Wait for your next round to pass; that extra round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect.”

requested_parts: multiple Infected scans without preexisting Larva
answers.answer: 1. No: if no Larva before Rest, multiple scanned Infected cards place just one Larva and do not kill. 2. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on board before it.

requested_parts: Noise roll location for remote Nest Egg attack

requested_parts: Scientist Intranet and Object outside Laboratory
answers.answer: 1. No. Scientist's Intranet does not bypass requirement that Object itself be in Laboratory; carrying Object elsewhere cannot reveal Weakness. 2. Research/Analyse keeps Object; only a corresponding Object in Laboratory reveals Weakness.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Storage Room Action can be used repeatedly at Item Counter zero, paying normal cost and Room restrictions. 2. Counter limits Search Action card; ordinary Search lowers counter by 1 and cannot be used at zero (except Scout Scavenging).

requested_parts: Nest Fire Egg destruction with Vulnerability
answers.answer: 1. Two Nest Eggs are destroyed during each Event Phase Fire Damage step when Nest is on Fire and Vulnerability to Fire is discovered.

requested_parts: drop carried Egg in Nest and Nest total

answers.answer: 1. Yes, Medkit may be used on another Character. 2. Yes, Bandages may be used on another Character.

answers.answer: 1. No Larva is placed when Alcohol scans an Infected Contamination card. 2. Instead, gain one new Contamination card.

requested_parts: Hand Serious Wound and Motion Scanner

Gain one new Contamination card; reshuffle it with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in hand. 4. You then pass; may keep hand cards. 5. Surgery also removes Larva and Infected cards, but scans all zones, shuffles entire hand too, gives no new Contamination and costs 1 Light Wound; automatically pass.

requested_parts: automatic Event Phase after one two-Action round per player
next-round order and size while players active
answers.answer: 1. No, Event Phase does not begin just because each player had one round. 2. Player rounds repeat in First Player order clockwise while any player has not passed; each round is 2 Actions. 3. A player who takes one Action must pass. 4. A player who cannot or chooses not to take any Actions must pass. 5. Passing players cannot take further normal Actions (but may play eligible Interruption); Player Phase ends once all players have passed, then Event Phase begins.
answers.evidence: [1] “Series of rounds repeat as long as at least one player has not passed.” [2] each performs “round of 2 Actions”; clockwise from First Player. [3] “If you perform only 1 Action instead of two, you must pass.” [4] “If you cannot perform any Actions, or choose not to, you must pass.” [5] rounds until “all players pass”; after passing no normal Actions; sequence then Event Phase.

answers.answer: 1. Canteen lets you Heal 1 Light Wound. 2. Shower lets you discard your Slime marker. 3. Each may also scan all Contamination cards in your hand as part of that Room Action; benefit and scan can both be taken. 4. You may take the non-scanning benefit without choosing to scan.
answers.evidence: [1] “Canteen — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan…” [2] “Shower Room — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan…” [3] “may also” confirms combined Room Action. [4] The “may also” scan is optional; base benefit stands independently.

answers.evidence: [1] “Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner”; unscanned cards remain unknown. [2] “place the Scanner’s red foil over the card’s coded text field”; “exact word INFECTED appears in one line.” [3] “A merely similar-looking coded word does not count.”
